memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses told his father-in-law about everything the LORD had done to Pharaoh and
the Egyptians for Israel's sake and about all the hardships they had met along
the way and how the LORD had saved them." - Ex 18:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses tells the whole story, and notice what he includes.

He tells what God did to Pharaoh. He tells "about all the hardships they had met
along the way." And he tells how the LORD saved them.

The hardships are in the middle of the testimony, not edited out of it. This is
honest storytelling. Moses does not present a clean narrative where God acts and
everything goes smoothly. There was bitter water, there was no water, there was
hunger, there was an army at Rephidim.

We often tell our stories the other way round, either all victory or all
struggle. The truthful version has both, and it is more useful to whoever is
listening. A testimony with no hardship in it leaves people feeling they are
doing something wrong when their own road is hard.

Notice how it ends, though: "how the LORD had saved them." The hardships are
told, but they are not the conclusion. God's faithfulness is.

That is the shape of an honest Christian testimony. Not "everything was fine,"
and not "everything was terrible," but "it was hard, and God was faithful."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you edit the hard parts out of your story?
2. Does your account of your life end with the difficulty or with God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, help me to tell the truth about my life, including the hard parts, and
to let the story end with Your faithfulness. Amen.
